claims.text: An equimolar noble-metal HEA composition maximizes configurational entropy during synthesis.
Higher configurational entropy promotes atomic homogeneity and minimizes short-range ordering.
Maximized configurational entropy facilitates complete atomic mixing and suppresses clustering and phase segregation.
A homogeneous atomic distribution produces uniformly distributed catalytic active sites.
Uniformly distributed active sites are more stable under ORR conditions and provide higher catalytic performance.
Reducing the content of one or two elements by 20–30% lowers configurational entropy relative to the equimolar composition.
The entropy reduction caused by a non-equimolar composition promotes atomic clustering or phase segregation.
Atomic clustering or phase segregation diminishes catalytic efficiency and durability.
Composition influences ORR activity and electrochemical stability in noble-metal HEAs.
The proposed controlled system is a Pt–Pd–Au–Ag–Rh nanoparticle HEA synthesized by one-pot colloidal reduction at approximately 180 °C.
EXAFS and atom-probe tomography can quantitatively distinguish atomic homogeneity and local short-range ordering in these nanoparticles.
Equimolar nanoparticles will have a narrower particle-size distribution than the non-equimolar baseline.
Equimolar nanoparticles will exhibit greater lattice distortion indicative of a true HEA phase.
Equimolar nanoparticles will have higher and more stable ORR activity than nanoparticles in which one or two elements are reduced by 20–30%.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to noble-metal HEA nanoparticles made by one-pot colloidal reduction near 180 °C and tested under controlled ORR conditions.
Synthesis kinetics can influence atomic distribution independently of configurational entropy.
Minor synthesis-parameter variations can alter the relationship between atomic homogeneity and catalytic performance.
